newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stays confident on its China investments.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stays confident on its China investments.

text.p: The government's Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Thursday it was confident that Singapore's investments in China would continue to grow despite the death of paramount Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.
"The EDB is confident that investments between China and Singapore will continue to grow," the EDB said in a written reply to a query from Reuters.

"As part of its ongoing efforts to participate in the tremendous growth in Asia-Pacific, the EDB, through its regionalisation programme, will continue to assist companies to venture into China and the region," the statement said.

The EDB said Singapore was the fifth-biggest investor in China, with total investment amounting to US$1.86 billion in 1995. Singapore companies invested a further $987 million in China in the first six months of 1996, it said.
The EDB is a government body formed to seek foreign investment at home and encourage local companies to venture abroad.
